1	# Data Lineage Trust Platform
2	
3	Backend service for managing datasets, their immutable schema versions and
4	field-level lineage between schema versions. All metadata is persisted in a
5	SQLite database, so data created before a restart remains queryable afterwards.
6	
7	## Requirements
8	
9	- Python 3.12+
10	
11	## Install and test
12	
13	```bash
14	python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'
15	python -m pytest
16	```
17	
18	## Start
19	
20	```bash
21	python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
22	```
23	
24	The SQLite database is stored at `data/lineage.db` by default. Override the
25	location with the `DATA_LINEAGE_DB` environment variable.
26	
27	## Public API
28	
29	All endpoints return JSON. Error responses use the stable shape
30	`{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<message>"}` and never expose SQL or stack
31	traces.
32	
33	### Health
34	
35	- `GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` when the service is ready.
36	
37	### Datasets
38	
39	- `POST /datasets` — create a dataset. Body: `{"name": "orders", "description": "optional"}`.
40	  Returns `201` with `id`, `name`, `description`, `created_at`. Empty name →
41	  `422`; duplicate name → `409`.
42	- `GET /datasets` — list all datasets.
43	
44	### Schema versions (immutable, numbered from 1 per dataset)
45	
46	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — create the next schema version. Body:
47	  `{"fields": [{"name": "id", "type": "integer", "nullable": false}]}`.
48	  Field list must be non-empty, field `name`/`type`/`nullable` are required and
49	  field names must be unique within the version. Unknown dataset → `404`;
50	  invalid fields → `422` (nothing is written).
51	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions` — list all versions of a dataset with
52	  their fields.
53	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}` — read one version with its
54	  fields. Unknown dataset/version → `404`.
55	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}` —
56	  read-only breaking-change check of the target version against the base
57	  version, computed fresh from the persisted field definitions on every read
58	  (nothing is written; field order is not a difference). The endpoint takes no
59	  request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version →
60	  `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the version diff. The JSON
61	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
62	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_version`, `target_version`,
63	  `breaking_changes` and `breaking_change_count`. A breaking change is exactly
64	  one of: the target removed a base field (`removed`), changed a field's type
65	  (`type_changed`) or tightened a nullable field to not nullable
66	  (`nullable_tightened`); added fields and nullable loosening are not
67	  breaking. Each entry has `field`, `kind`, `before` (base definition) and
68	  `after` (target definition, `null` for a removed field), entries are sorted
69	  by field name ascending and `breaking_change_count` equals the number of
70	  entries. Comparing a version with itself returns an empty list and a zero
71	  count. The verdict is advisory for release decisions only: it runs no
72	  migration or rollback.
73	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{base_version}/compatibility/{target_version}/impact` —
74	  read-only companion of the compatibility check: the same top-level keys
75	  (`base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_changes`,
76	  `breaking_change_count`) and the same breaking entries, each entry carrying
77	  one extra key `impacted` after `after`. `impacted` lists every field
78	  directly or indirectly downstream of the broken field along the lineage
79	  mappings, starting from the base version's same-named field and — when the
80	  field still exists in the target version — also from the target version's
81	  field. Each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`; the set is
82	  deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate) and is
83	  sorted by dataset, version and field ascending. A field with no downstream
84	  yields an empty list. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
85	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404` with the same
86	  404-before-422 precedence as the compatibility check, and the JSON document
87	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
88	  newline). The read is fully side-effect free: version definitions, lineage
89	  mappings and the impact cache are never written.
90	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/evolution-summary` — read-only whole-dataset
91	  summary of adjacent-version breaking changes and their downstream impact,
92	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version
93	  definitions, lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched).
94	  Quality and privacy state play no role. The path carries only the dataset
95	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an unknown
96	  dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
97	  compatibility reads. A dataset with fewer than two versions returns `200`
98	  with an empty `pairs` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
99	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
100	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`, `pairs` and `totals`.
101	  `pairs` is ordered by base version number ascending and lists every
102	  adjacent version pair, including pairs without breaking changes; each entry
103	  has exactly `base_version`, `target_version`, `breaking_count`,
104	  `impacted_count` and `impacted_datasets` in that order. `breaking_count` is
105	  the number of breaking entries of the pair, judged exactly as in the
106	  pairwise compatibility impact response (`removed`, `type_changed` or
107	  `nullable_tightened`; several changes of one field collapse into a single
108	  entry). The pair's impacted set is the union of every breaking entry's
109	  downstream fields — same start-field rule as the pairwise impact response,
110	  merged and deduplicated, never containing a start field itself (cycles
111	  terminate) — `impacted_count` is its size and `impacted_datasets` lists the
112	  distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. `totals` has
113	  exactly `pair_count` (the number of pairs), `breaking_count` and
114	  `impacted_count`, each the sum of the per-pair values over the whole
115	  dataset.
116	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/fields/{field}/trajectory` — read-only
117	  cross-version trajectory of one named field of the dataset, computed fresh
118	  on every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions,
119	  lineage mappings and the impact cache are never touched). Only the
120	  persisted version field definitions and lineage mappings are read; quality,
121	  privacy, snapshot and processing-task state play no role. The path carries
122	  the dataset name and the field name; the request takes no body and no query
123	  parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, and a field that does not
124	  appear in any of the dataset's versions → `404`, both with the same
125	  404-before-422 precedence as the evolution summary. A dataset with fewer
126	  than two versions returns `200` with an empty `changes` array, never an
127	  error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
128	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
129	  `field`, `entries` and `changes` in that order. `entries` lists every
130	  schema version of the dataset ordered by version number ascending; each
131	  entry has exactly `version` and `definition`, where `definition` is the
132	  field's persisted definition in that version (`type` and `nullable` only)
133	  or `null` — the key is never omitted — when the field does not exist
134	  there. `changes` lists one entry per adjacent version pair, ordered by
135	  base version ascending; each entry has exactly `base_version`,
136	  `target_version`, `status`, `impacted` and `impacted_datasets` in that
137	  order. `status` reuses the breaking-entry vocabulary of the compatibility
138	  check — `added` (the field appears on the target side), `removed` (it
139	  disappears on the target side), `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened` —
140	  extended with `nullable_loosened` (only the nullability relaxes) and
141	  `unchanged` (both definitions agree, including both absent); a field that
142	  both changes type and tightens nullability collapses into a single
143	  `type_changed` status. `impacted` lists every field directly or indirectly
144	  downstream of the tracked field for that pair along the lineage mappings,
145	  with the same start-field rule as the pairwise compatibility impact
146	  response (the base version's same-named field and, when it exists, the
147	  target version's); each item is `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`, the set
148	  is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself (cycles terminate),
149	  is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending and is empty when the
150	  field has no downstream. `impacted_datasets` lists the distinct dataset
151	  names appearing in `impacted`, sorted ascending.
152	
153	### Field-level lineage
154	
155	A lineage link maps one field of a target schema version to one field of a
156	schema version in a different (source) dataset.
157	
158	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — register a mapping.
159	  Body names both ends:
160	
161	  ```json
162	  {
163	    "target_dataset": "dm_orders",
164	    "target_version": 1,
165	    "target_field": "id",
166	    "source_dataset": "raw_orders",
167	    "source_version": 1,
168	    "source_field": "order_id"
169	  }
170	  ```
171	
172	  Target must match the path. Source and target datasets must differ and every
173	  referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404` / `422` otherwise).
174	  Submitting the same complete mapping twice returns `409`.
175	- `DELETE /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — remove one
176	  registered mapping. Same address and same body shape as registration: the
177	  six locating fields name the complete mapping to delete and the body target
178	  must match the path. Every locating value readable in the request is
179	  resolved first, so an unknown dataset, version or field is a `404` ahead of
180	  every request-shape error; when all six values name existing resources but
181	  the mapping itself was never registered, the delete is likewise a `404`.
182	  An empty or whitespace body, invalid JSON, a non-object payload, missing or
183	  extra fields, wrongly typed values, blank names, any query parameter, a
184	  mapping whose source and target datasets coincide or whose body target
185	  disagrees with the path are all `422`. No rejection changes the lineage
186	  graph, the impact cache or any other metadata. A registered mapping is
187	  deleted atomically and returns `200` with the removed mapping in the
188	  registration response shape; concurrent deletes of the same mapping succeed
189	  exactly once (the loser gets `404` and changes nothing). The deletion is
190	  visible to every lineage read immediately and survives restarts; the cached
191	  impacts of the mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it
192	  are invalidated exactly as on registration, unrelated entries are kept.
193	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage` — return every target
194	  field (including fields without sources) together with its source references.
195	  Results are sorted by target field name, then source dataset name, source
196	  version and source field name.
197	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact?field=<field>` —
198	  return the downstream impact of one source field. The path and the `field`
199	  query parameter together name an existing field; the response is
200	  `{"source": {...}, "impacted": [...]}` where `impacted` lists every field
201	  reachable from the source along lineage mappings (direct and indirect), each
202	  entry being `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. Results are deduplicated,
203	  never contain the source itself (cycles terminate) and are sorted by dataset,
204	  version and field ascending. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; a
205	  missing, blank, invalid or repeated `field` parameter → `422` (a repeated
206	  `field` is judged before the field lookup, so it is always a `422`, never a
207	  field `404`).
208	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit` —
209	  read-only consistency audit of the version's impact cache, appended one
210	  segment after the impact query address. The path dataset and version name
211	  the audit scope; every field of that version is checked against its current
212	  cache record and recomputed fresh from the committed lineage graph using
213	  exactly the impact-query semantics (downstream fields merged and
214	  deduplicated, the start field excluded, cycles terminating). Each entry is
215	  `{"field", "status"}` with `cached` (the stored record equals the
216	  recomputed result), `missing` (no cache record because the field's impact
217	  was never queried — a normal state, not an error) or `mismatch` (the stored
218	  record differs). Entries are sorted by field name ascending and the sort
219	  does not depend on database order. The JSON document is deterministic
220	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with
221	  top-level keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order;
222	  `counts` gives `cached_count`, `missing_count` and `mismatch_count`, each
223	  equal to the number of entries with that status. The audit is computed on
224	  every read and never writes: no cache record is inserted, invalidated or
225	  repaired, so impact queries, impact paths and source paths behave exactly
226	  as before. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters; any
227	  body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an
228	  unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over
229	  `422` as in the impact query.
230	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-audit/repair`
231	  — controlled repair of the version's impact cache, appended one segment
232	  after the read-only audit address and accepting POST only. Every field of
233	  the version is recomputed against the committed lineage graph with the
234	  exact impact-query semantics: a field without a cache record gets one
235	  (`created`), a stored record that disagrees is rewritten (`updated`) and a
236	  matching record is left untouched (`unchanged`). Entries are sorted by
237	  field name ascending and the JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
238	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level
239	  keys `dataset`, `version`, `entries` and `counts` in that order; each
240	  entry has exactly `field` and `action`, and `counts` gives
241	  `created_count`, `updated_count` and `unchanged_count`. Written records

243	  surviving restarts; a subsequent audit reports every field as `cached`.
244	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters — any body
245	  bytes (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, an unknown

250	  explanations, source-path reads and the read-only audit are unaffected.
251	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact/cache-invalidations`

266	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
267	  `version` and `entries` in that order. The trail is append-only and
268	  survives restarts; the read only reads persisted records and never writes,
269	  invalidates or repairs anything. The endpoint takes no request body and no
270	  query parameters; any body bytes (whitespace-only included) or query
271	  parameter → `422`, and an unknown dataset or version → `404`, with `404`
272	  taking precedence over `422` as in the impact query.
273	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/lineage/impact-paths?field=<field>` —
274	  read-only shortest-path explanation of the same impact, computed fresh on
275	  every read (no caching; nothing is written, and version definitions, lineage
276	  mappings and the impact cache are never touched). The path and the `field`
277	  query parameter together name an existing field. The JSON document is
278	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
279	  newline) with top-level keys `source`, `impacts`, `direct_count` and
280	  `indirect_count` in that order; `source` is the start field reference

312	  shortest node sequence walking from the start field up to the origin,
313	  including both ends, and each node has the same
314	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}` shape; `path_length` is the number of
315	  edges on the path (`1` for a direct source, increasing for indirect ones).
316	  Among several shortest paths, the lexicographically smallest node sequence
317	  (compared by dataset, version and field) is chosen; cycles terminate.
318	  `direct_count` counts origins at distance 1, `indirect_count` the origins
319	  farther away and `source_dataset_count` the distinct dataset names among
320	  all origins; a field with no sources returns an empty `origins` array and
321	  all counts zero, never an error. The endpoint takes no request body and no
322	  query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or repeated `field` is
323	  likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field → `404`, with `404`
324	  taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated `field` is judged
325	  before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
326	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/lineage-coverage` — read-only whole-dataset check
327	  reporting, for every schema version at once, how the version's fields are
328	  covered by registered lineage mappings. Versions are sorted by version
329	  number ascending and a dataset without versions returns an empty `versions`
330	  array, never an error. Each version entry has exactly `version`, `fields`,
331	  `linked_field_count`, `unlinked_field_count` and `mapping_count` in that
332	  order; `fields` lists every field of the version sorted by field name, each
333	  entry having exactly `field`, `sources` and `source_dataset_count`.
334	  `sources` lists every mapping source registered with the field as its
335	  target; each reference has the location keys `dataset`, `version` and
336	  `field` in that order, is deduplicated and sorted by those three keys
337	  ascending, and the sort never depends on database order. A field without a
338	  source is listed all the same with an empty `sources` array and a
339	  `source_dataset_count` of zero; that count counts the distinct source
340	  dataset names among the references, never the number of mappings.
341	  `mapping_count` equals the sum of the fields' source-reference counts and
342	  `linked_field_count` plus `unlinked_field_count` equals the number of
343	  fields. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
344	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
345	  `versions` and `totals` in that order; `totals` gives `version_count`,
346	  `field_count`, `linked_field_count`, `unlinked_field_count` and
347	  `mapping_count`, each equal to the sum of the matching per-version values
348	  (all zero for a dataset without versions). The check is recomputed on
349	  every read and never writes: lineage mappings and the impact cache are
350	  never inserted, invalidated, repaired or otherwise touched. The endpoint
351	  takes no request body and no query parameters; any body bytes
352	  (whitespace-only included) or query parameter → `422`, and an unknown
353	  dataset → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over the shape checks.
354	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/lineage-source-coverage` — read-only whole-dataset
355	  source-side companion of the lineage coverage check, reporting, for every
356	  schema version at once, how the version's fields are registered as the
357	  source end of lineage mappings. Versions are sorted by version number
358	  ascending and a dataset without versions returns an empty `versions`
359	  array, never an error. Each version entry has exactly `version`, `fields`,
360	  `referenced_field_count`, `unreferenced_field_count` and `mapping_count`
361	  in that order; `fields` lists every field of the version sorted by field
362	  name, each entry having exactly `field`, `downstreams` and
363	  `downstream_dataset_count`. `downstreams` lists every mapping target
364	  registered with the field as its source; each reference has the location
365	  keys `dataset`, `version` and `field` in that order, is deduplicated and
366	  sorted by those three keys ascending, and the sort never depends on
367	  database order. A field without a downstream is listed all the same with
368	  an empty `downstreams` array and a `downstream_dataset_count` of zero;
369	  that count counts the distinct target dataset names among the references,
370	  never the number of mappings. `mapping_count` equals the sum of the
371	  fields' downstream-reference counts and `referenced_field_count` plus
372	  `unreferenced_field_count` equals the number of fields. The JSON document
373	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
374	  trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`, `versions` and `totals`
375	  in that order; `totals` gives `version_count`, `field_count`,
376	  `referenced_field_count`, `unreferenced_field_count` and `mapping_count`,
377	  each equal to the sum of the matching per-version values (all zero for a
378	  dataset without versions). The check is recomputed on every read and
379	  never writes: lineage mappings and the impact cache are never inserted,
380	  invalidated, repaired or otherwise touched, and the target-side lineage
381	  coverage read behaves exactly as before. The endpoint takes no request
382	  body and no query parameters; any body bytes (whitespace-only and a
383	  single space included) or query parameter → `422`, and an unknown
384	  dataset → `404`, with `404` taking precedence over the shape checks.
385	
386	  Impact results are cached persistently (they survive restarts) and every
387	  read reflects the currently committed lineage graph: creating a schema
388	  version invalidates the cache entries related to that dataset, and creating
389	  or deleting a lineage mapping invalidates the cached impacts of the
390	  mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it. Unrelated
391	  cache entries are preserved.

393	### Quality rules
394	
395	Quality rules validate rows against a schema version. Rules are version-scoped
396	and persisted (including their enabled state) across restarts.
397	
398	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — create a rule.
399	  Body: `{"name": "id required", "kind": "not_null", "params": {...}}`. Returns
400	  `201` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `params`, `enabled`, `created_at`; `enabled`
401	  defaults to `true`. Rule names must be unique within a version (`409` on
402	  conflict). Referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404`); other invalid
403	  input returns `422` and nothing is written. Supported kinds:
404	  - `not_null` — params `{"field": "<existing field>"}`.
405	  - `numeric_range` — params `{"field": "<existing field>", "min": <finite
406	    number>, "max": <finite number>}` with `min <= max`.
407	  - `unique` — params `{"fields": ["<existing field>", ...]}`: a non-empty list
408	    of distinct, existing field names.
409	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — list rules
410	  sorted by `id` ascending.
411	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/{rule_id}` —
412	  enable or disable a rule. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
413	  the updated rule. Unknown rule/dataset/version → `404`.
414	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluate` —
415	  evaluate rows. Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}`. Only enabled rules run.
416	  Returns `{"dataset", "version", "results"}` with results sorted by `rule_id`;
417	  each result has `rule_id`, `name`, `passed` and `violations` (0-based row
418	  indices in ascending order).
419	  - `not_null` fails on missing or `null` values.
420	  - `numeric_range` fails on missing, `null`, non-numeric, boolean or
421	    out-of-range values (boundaries included).
422	  - `unique` compares the tuple of `fields` values per row; a missing field
423	    counts as `null`, and every row taking part in a duplicate group is a
424	    violation.
425	  - With an empty `rows` list every rule passes.
426	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations` —
427	  list the persisted evaluation history of the version, ordered by `sequence`
428	  (occurrence order). Every successful evaluation appends one immutable
429	  summary (`sequence`, `dataset`, `version`, `row_count`,
430	  `violation_row_count` — the number of distinct submitted rows violating at
431	  least one rule — `results` and `created_at`); rejected or failed
432	  evaluations leave no record, and an empty `rows` submission is recorded
433	  with zero violations. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
434	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
435	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/at?timestamp=...`
436	  — read-only point-in-time single-record look-back, appended one segment
437	  after the evaluation history address and accepting GET only. `timestamp`
438	  must be a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`);
439	  only evaluation summaries written at or before it form the look-back
440	  window, and the returned summary is the window's highest-sequence record
441	  in exactly the single-record shape of the history (`sequence`, `dataset`,
442	  `version`, `row_count`, `violation_row_count`, `results`, `created_at`).
443	  A window with no recorded evaluation is a normal response, not an error:
444	  the same key set is still returned with `sequence`, `row_count`,
445	  `violation_row_count` and `created_at` set to null (keys are never
446	  omitted) and `results` an empty list. Only persisted evaluation summaries
447	  are read: rules are never re-run, history summaries are never rewritten,
448	  nothing is cached or written, and the window grows naturally as new
449	  evaluations are persisted, so the same data yields the same document byte
450	  for byte across process restarts, and the ordering of rule results never
451	  depends on database natural order. The JSON document is deterministic
452	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline). The
453	  path dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
454	  bytes (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
455	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
456	  writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}` shape without
457	  exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the evaluation history,
458	  the pairwise and point-in-time diffs and every other endpoint are
459	  unchanged.
460	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff`
461	  — read-only diff between the two most recent recorded evaluations
462	  (`from_sequence` → `to_sequence`). `added_violation_rows` /
463	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
464	  stopped violating any rule, and each entry of `rules` carries the rule's
465	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
466	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
467	  `violation_count_delta` (negative, zero or positive). A rule missing from
468	  one side (disabled or created between the two evaluations) has a `null`
469	  side and `null` row-level diff fields. With fewer than two recorded
470	  evaluations the response is an explicit empty result (null sequences,
471	  empty lists), not an error. The path dataset/version resolves first
472	  (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) or
473	  any query parameter are a `422` that writes nothing.
474	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff/at?timestamp=...`
475	  — read-only point-in-time companion of the evaluation diff, appended one
476	  segment after the pairwise diff address and accepting GET only.
477	  `timestamp` must be a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or
478	  trailing `Z`); only evaluation summaries written at or before it count as
479	  the look-back window, and the two that participate are the window's
480	  highest-sequence pair — the newest is `to`, its predecessor `from`. The
481	  comparison is exactly the pairwise diff's: `added_violation_rows` /
482	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
483	  stopped violating any rule, and each `rules` entry carries the rule's
484	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
485	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
486	  `violation_count_delta`. A rule missing from one side (disabled or created
487	  between the two evaluations) has a `null` side and `null` row-level diff
488	  fields — the key is never omitted. A window with fewer than two recorded
489	  evaluations returns the same explicit empty result as the pairwise diff
490	  (null sequences, empty lists), not an error. Only persisted evaluation
491	  summaries are read: rules are never re-run, history summaries are never
492	  rewritten, nothing is cached or written, and the window grows naturally as
493	  new evaluations are persisted, so the same data yields the same document
494	  byte for byte across process restarts. The JSON document is deterministic
495	  (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline). The
496	  path dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
497	  bytes (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
498	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
499	  writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}` shape without
500	  exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the evaluation history,
501	  the pairwise diff and every other endpoint are unchanged.
502	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/trend`
503	  — read-only trend summary, appended one segment after the evaluation
504	  history address and accepting GET only. The caller sends no request body
505	  and no query parameter. The summary is computed fresh from the persisted
506	  evaluation history on every read: rules are never re-run, history
507	  summaries are never rewritten, nothing is cached or written, and the same
508	  history yields the same document byte for byte across process restarts,
509	  with every ordering explicit rather than dependent on database natural
510	  order.
511	  - `evaluations` lists one entry per evaluation ordered by ascending
512	    `sequence`, each carrying the history summary's `created_at` (write
513	    time), `row_count` (submitted rows) and `violation_row_count`, plus
514	    `violation_row_count_delta` — the change in violation row count against
515	    the previous evaluation; on the first evaluation it is `null` and the
516	    key is never omitted.
517	  - `rules` gives one row per rule that appears in the history, sorted by
518	    rule id ascending, including rules that have since been disabled and
519	    rules that never recorded a violation. Each row carries `rule_id` and
520	    `name`, the cumulative `violation_row_count` (summed over evaluations),
521	    the `violating_evaluation_count`, and `first_violation_sequence` /
522	    `last_violation_sequence` — the sequences of the rule's first and last
523	    violating evaluation, both `null` (never omitted) when the rule never
524	    violated; its counts are zero in that case.
525	  - `totals` reports the whole-version `evaluation_count`, the
526	    `violation_row_count` total (the sum of the per-evaluation counts) and
527	    the `rule_count` of distinct rules the history involves. An empty
528	    history is an explicit empty result (empty `evaluations` and `rules`,
529	    all-zero totals), returned normally rather than as an error.
530	  - The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact
531	    whitespace, lowercase booleans, exactly one trailing newline). The path
532	    dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body
533	    bytes (whitespace-only included) or any query parameter are a `422`
534	    that writes nothing. Errors keep the stable `{"error", "detail"}`
535	    shape without exposing SQL, stack traces or internal objects; the
536	    evaluation history, the pairwise and point-in-time diffs, anomaly
537	    detection and every other endpoint are unchanged.

539	### Quality anomaly detection
540	
541	Anomaly detection runs over the persisted evaluation history of a schema
542	version. A version carries at most one detection config; scans append
543	immutable anomaly records that persist across restarts.
544	
545	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
546	  — register the version's detection config. The body contains exactly three
547	  integers: `consecutive_worsening_steps` (at least `2`),
548	  `violation_row_limit` and `rule_violation_limit` (both non-negative).
549	  Returns `201` with the config (`id`, `dataset`, `version`, the three
550	  thresholds, `created_at`). A second config for the same version returns
551	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing, extra, non-integer or
552	  out-of-range fields → `422` and nothing is written.
553	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
554	  — return the registered config (`404` when none exists). The endpoint takes
555	  no request body and no query parameters (`422`).
556	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/scan`
557	  — run one detection pass over the persisted evaluation history and return
558	  the anomaly records this scan newly added (ordered by `id`); they are
559	  persisted in the same transaction. Scanning without a registered config
560	  returns `409`; an empty history is a successful scan that writes nothing.
561	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`). Each
562	  record has `id`, `kind`, `sequence` (the history sequence it points to),
563	  `rule_id`, `violation_count` and `created_at`; `kind` is one of:
564	  - `row_limit` — the evaluation's `violation_row_count` exceeds
565	    `violation_row_limit` (`rule_id` is `null`).
566	  - `rule_limit` — one rule's violation count in the evaluation exceeds
567	    `rule_violation_limit`; `rule_id` carries the rule's id.
568	  - `trend` — the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations strictly
569	    increase and the consecutive increase count at the tail of the history
570	    reaches `consecutive_worsening_steps`; the record points to the final
571	    evaluation of the increasing sequence (`rule_id` is `null`). A shorter
572	    run or any decline produces no trend record.
573	
574	  A record with the same kind, history sequence and rule id is never
575	  duplicated: repeated scans only persist and return newly appearing
576	  anomalies, and concurrent scans store each anomaly exactly once with
577	  contiguous ids.
578	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/anomalies`
579	  — list every anomaly record of the version sorted by `id` ascending (empty
580	  when there are none, never an error). Same `404`/`422` rules as the scan
581	  endpoint; nothing is written.

583	### Quality gate
584	
585	The quality gate is the release-readiness verdict of a schema version. It is
586	computed fresh from the persisted records on every read — nothing is cached,
587	re-run or written, and the rule definitions are never consulted (violations
588	recorded for rules since disabled still count).
589	
590	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate` — return the
591	  verdict as a deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact
592	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
593	  `{"dataset", "version", "verdict", "reasons", "counts"}`.
594	  - `verdict` is one of:
595	    - `pass` — the latest recorded evaluation passed every rule and no
596	      anomaly record exists; a zero-violation evaluation left by an empty
597	      `rows` submission is a valid basis.
598	    - `undetermined` — no evaluation was ever recorded; `reasons` is empty
599	      and the read succeeds (never an error).
600	    - `fail` — the latest recorded evaluation still has violating rows, or
601	      the version carries any anomaly record.
602	  - `reasons` lists every factor that lowers the verdict, sorted by `kind`,
603	    `sequence` and `rule_id` (null ids first), all ascending. Each reason has
604	    `kind`, `sequence`, `rule_id` and `violation_count` (a missing rule id is
605	    `null`, never omitted). Every rule with violations in the latest
606	    evaluation contributes one `violation` reason with its violation row
607	    count; every persisted anomaly record contributes one reason of its own
608	    kind (`row_limit`, `rule_limit` or `trend`). A rule that appears in both
609	    yields two reasons — they are never merged or deduplicated.
610	  - `counts` reports how many persisted records the verdict examined:
611	    `evaluations`, `anomalies` and `reasons` (the length of the reason list).
612	  - The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters: any body
613	    bytes — including whitespace-only ones — or any query parameter are a
614	    `422`, checked after the path dataset/version resolves (`404` first).
615	    Nothing is written on any rejection.
616	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate/at?timestamp=...`
617	  — the same verdict as it stood at a requested instant. `timestamp` must be
618	  a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time; only evaluations and anomaly records
619	  written at or before it count, and the latest evaluation of that window is
620	  the one with the highest sequence inside it. The response is the same
621	  deterministic document as the bare gate (`dataset`, `version`, `verdict`,
622	  `reasons`, `counts`, one trailing newline), with the counts covering only
623	  the records inside the window. A window without any evaluation is
624	  `undetermined` with an empty reason list — a normal response, never an
625	  error. The endpoint accepts GET only and is strictly read-only. The path
626	  dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes
627	  (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
628	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
629	  writes nothing.
630	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/quality-gate-export` — read-only cross-version
631	  export of the dataset's whole quality gate state, computed fresh on every
632	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no
633	  evaluation, anomaly record or gate verdict is touched). The path carries
634	  only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no query parameters —
635	  any body bytes, including a purely whitespace or single-space body, or any
636	  query parameter → `422`; an unknown dataset → `404`, checked before the
637	  request shape, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the compliance
638	  exports. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an empty
639	  `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON document is
640	  deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
641	  newline):
642	
643	  ```json
644	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"verdict":"fail","reason_count":1,"violation_row_count":2},{"version":2,"verdict":"undetermined","reason_count":0,"violation_row_count":null}],"totals":{"version_count":2,"failed_count":1,"reason_count":1,"violation_row_count":2}}
645	  ```
646	
647	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
648	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry has
649	  exactly `version`, `verdict`, `reason_count` and `violation_row_count` in
650	  that order. `verdict` is the current per-version gate verdict (one of
651	  `pass`, `undetermined`, `fail`) under exactly the same computation as the
652	  per-version gate read; `reason_count` is the number of reasons currently
653	  lowering that verdict (the length of the per-version gate's reason list);
654	  `violation_row_count` is the violation row count of the latest recorded
655	  evaluation and is `null` — never omitted — when the version was never
656	  evaluated. `totals` has exactly `version_count`, `failed_count`,
657	  `reason_count` and `violation_row_count`: the number of version entries,
658	  the number of versions whose verdict is `fail`, and the sums of the
659	  per-version reason and violation row counts (null violation row counts
660	  count as zero).
661	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/quality-rule-coverage` — read-only cross-version
662	  check of how the dataset's schema fields are covered by quality rules,
663	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
664	  deleted, and no rule definition or evaluation record is touched). The path
665	  carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no query
666	  parameters — any body bytes, including a purely whitespace or single-space
667	  body, or any query parameter → `422`; an unknown dataset → `404`, checked
668	  before the request shape, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
669	  compliance exports. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
670	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
671	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
672	  trailing newline; the same data renders byte-identically after a process
673	  restart and ordering never depends on the database's natural order):
674	
675	  ```json
676	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[{"field":"amount","coverage":"disabled","kinds":["numeric_range"],"rule_ids":[3]},{"field":"id","coverage":"enabled","kinds":["not_null","unique"],"rule_ids":[1,2]},{"field":"region","coverage":"unregistered","kinds":null,"rule_ids":null}]}],"totals":{"version_count":1,"field_count":3,"enabled_count":1,"disabled_count":1,"unregistered_count":1}}
677	  ```
678	
679	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
680	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry has
681	  exactly `version` and `fields`, with every field of the version listed by
682	  field name ascending. Each field entry has exactly `field`, `coverage`,
683	  `kinds` and `rule_ids` in that order. `coverage` is one of the literals
684	  `enabled` (at least one enabled rule references the field), `disabled`
685	  (rules reference the field but all of them are disabled) and
686	  `unregistered` (no rule references the field). `kinds` is the
687	  de-duplicated list of referencing rule kinds sorted by literal value and
688	  `rule_ids` the referencing rules' ids de-duplicated and sorted ascending;
689	  every field of a unique rule counts as referenced. When a field is also
690	  referenced by disabled rules alongside enabled ones, their kinds and ids
691	  are included too. For an `unregistered` field both `kinds` and `rule_ids`
692	  are `null` — the keys are never omitted. `totals` has exactly
693	  `version_count`, `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count` and
694	  `unregistered_count`: each is the sum of the per-version entries, and the
695	  field count equals the sum of the three per-state counts.

697	### Privacy policies
698	
699	Privacy policies attach a sensitivity classification and masking strategy to a
700	single field of a schema version, enabling role-based de-identification of row
701	data. Policies (including their enabled state) are persisted across restarts.
702	
703	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — register a
704	  policy. Body:
705	  `{"field": "email", "classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles": ["analyst"]}`.
706	  `field` must name an existing field of the version; `classification` is a
707	  non-empty string; `masking` is `redact` or `partial`; `allowed_roles` is an
708	  array of distinct, non-empty role names and may be empty. Returns `201` with
709	  the submitted fields plus `id`, `enabled` (defaults to `true`) and
710	  `created_at`. Registering two policies for the same field within one version
711	  returns `409`. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; other invalid input →
712	  `422` and nothing is written.
713	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — list policies
714	  sorted by `id` ascending.
715	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
716	  enable or disable a policy. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
717	  the updated policy. Unknown policy/dataset/version → `404`.
718	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
719	  revise a policy. Body carries exactly the three adjustable fields:
720	  `{"classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles":
721	  ["analyst"]}`, using the same value rules as registration — a non-empty
722	  `classification` after trimming, `masking` of `redact` or `partial`, and an
723	  `allowed_roles` array of distinct, non-empty-after-trimming role names that
724	  may be empty. The three fields are replaced together from one whole
725	  submission. The revision never changes the policy id, the field it belongs
726	  to, its `enabled` state or its `created_at`; it writes only the policy
727	  itself — no policy is created, no identification record is touched and no
728	  masking suggestion is registered. Returns `200` with the updated policy in
729	  the same shape as the policy read, and the revision survives restarts. The
730	  next privacy view read (and every later masked read) judges each value by
731	  the revised classification, masking and allowed roles. Already-written
732	  masking-hit records, access records and cleanup requests are unaffected —
733	  their contents and ordering stay as written; the grouping of the summary,
734	  diff and reconciliation responses keeps the same counting rules, while the
735	  policy classification and masking reported on trend rows (and the policy
736	  entries of the coverage check and compliance export) reflect the current
737	  values. Advisory masking suggestions are unaffected. Unknown
738	  dataset/version/policy → `404`, judged before every request-shape check;
739	  missing or extra fields, a blank `classification`, an illegal `masking`
740	  value, duplicate or blank `allowed_roles` entries, an empty or
741	  whitespace-only body, malformed JSON, a non-object payload or any query
742	  parameter → `422` and nothing is written. Concurrent revisions of the same
743	  policy have exactly one winner; the loser receives `409` and changes no
744	  field.
745	
746	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view` — return a
747	  role-scoped, order-preserving copy of submitted rows. Body:
748	  `{"role": "guest", "rows": [{...}, ...]}` with a non-empty `role` and a list
749	  of row objects. Response: `{"dataset", "version", "rows"}`. Only enabled
750	  policies whose field appears in a row mask the value when `role` is not in
751	  `allowed_roles`:
752	  - `redact` replaces every non-`null` value with `"***"`.
753	  - `partial` keeps the first character and last two characters of strings
754	    longer than 4 characters (e.g. `"alice@example.com"` → `"aom"`); every other
755	    non-`null` value (short strings, numbers, booleans, …) is replaced with
756	    `"***"`.
757	  - `null` values and fields without a policy are returned unchanged; rows
758	    missing a covered field are left without it.
759	
760	  Every successful view also appends one audit record per value it actually
761	  masked (the same field masked in several rows yields one record per masked
762	  value; a role in `allowed_roles`, a `null` value, an uncovered field or a
763	  disabled policy never hits); the records are persisted per version and are
764	  append-only.
765	
766	  Every successful view additionally appends exactly one access record,
767	  whether or not it masked any value (an empty `rows` submission is recorded
768	  too). Rejected or failed views leave neither kind of record.
769	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/access-records`
770	  — list every access record of the version, ordered by `sequence` ascending
771	  (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has `sequence`,
772	  `role`, `row_count` (the number of submitted rows), `masked_count` (the
773	  number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
774	  cross-check) and `created_at`. The endpoint takes no request body and no
775	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is
776	  written.
777	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records`
778	  — list every masking-hit record of the version, ordered by `sequence`
779	  ascending (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has
780	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`. The
781	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
782	  dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is written.
783	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/search`
784	  — read-only filtered retrieval of the same masking-hit records. The
785	  response is the same record collection as the full list (each record has
786	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`),
787	  sorted by `sequence` ascending; a filter that matches nothing returns an
788	  empty array, never an error. All filters are optional query parameters and
789	  combine with AND:
790	  - `role` — exact match against the requesting role recorded on the hit,
791	    case-insensitive (no substring or other fuzzy matching).
792	  - `field` — exact match against the hit field name, case-insensitive.
793	  - `start` / `end` — closed write-time interval: a record matches when its
794	    `created_at` is between the bounds inclusive. Each bound is a
795	    timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`); either bound may be
796	    given alone. `start` later than `end` → `422`.
797	
798	  The endpoint takes no request body; an unparseable or timezone-less
799	  `start`/`end`, or any query parameter other than `role`, `field`, `start`
800	  and `end`, → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
801	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list. It is strictly read-only:
802	  no record is written, modified or deleted and the summary/diff responses
803	  are unaffected.
804	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/summary`
805	  — read-only compliance summary computed fresh from the persisted records on
806	  every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted). Response:
807	  `{"dataset", "version", "groups"}`; `groups` is an empty array when the
808	  version has no records. Each group merges records with the same `field`,
809	  `policy_id`, `role` and `masking` (different roles or masking modes stay
810	  separate) and lists `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking`, `hit_count`
811	  (one record counts as one hit), `first_hit_at` and `last_hit_at` (the
812	  earliest and latest record `created_at` in the group). Groups sort by
813	  `field`, then `policy_id`, `role` and `masking`, all ascending. The
814	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
815	  dataset/version → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
816	  record list.
817	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/trend`
818	  — read-only hit trend aggregated by privacy policy, computed fresh from the
819	  persisted records on every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted).
820	  Hits of the same policy merge across roles (a disabled policy's historical
821	  hits still count). Response: `{"dataset", "version", "policies", "totals"}`;
822	  `policies` is an empty array when the version has no records. Each policy
823	  row carries `policy_id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `total_hits`
824	  and `days`; policies sort by `policy_id` ascending. `days` lists only UTC
825	  calendar days with hits (a write time with a non-zero offset buckets by its
826	  UTC day), sorted ascending with no zero-filled gaps; each entry has `day`
827	  (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `hit_count` (one record counts once), `hit_count_delta`
828	  (difference from the previous listed day, `null` on the first) and `trend`
829	  (`up`/`down`/`flat`, or `none` on the first day). `totals` gives
830	  `total_hits` (the sum of the row totals), `policy_count` (policies with
831	  hits) and `day_count` (distinct hit days over the whole version, the
832	  per-policy day union). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
833	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
834	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
835	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
836	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
837	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
838	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
839	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
840	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
841	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
842	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
843	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
844	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
845	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
846	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
847	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
848	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
849	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
850	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
851	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
852	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
853	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
854	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
855	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
856	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
857	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
858	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
859	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
860	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
861	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
862	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
863	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
864	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
865	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
866	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
867	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
868	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
869	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
870	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
871	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
872	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
873	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
874	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
875	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
876	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
877	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
878	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
879	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
880	  `409`.
881	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
882	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
883	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
884	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
885	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
886	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
887	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
888	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
889	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
890	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
891	
892	  ```json
893	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
894	  ```
895	
896	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
897	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
898	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
899	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
900	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
901	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
902	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
903	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
904	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
905	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
906	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
907	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
908	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
909	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
910	  values over the whole dataset.
911	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
912	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
913	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
914	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
915	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
916	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
917	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
918	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
919	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
920	  one trailing newline):
921	
922	  ```json
923	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
924	  ```
925	
926	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
927	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
928	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
929	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
930	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
931	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
932	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
933	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
934	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
935	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
936	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
937	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
938	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
939	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
940	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
941	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
942	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
943	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
944	  whole dataset.
945	
946	### Sensitive-field identification
947	
948	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
949	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
950	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
951	stable ids) persist across restarts.
952	
953	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
954	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
955	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
956	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
957	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
958	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
959	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
960	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
961	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
962	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
963	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
964	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
965	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
966	
967	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
968	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
969	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
970	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
971	
972	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
973	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
974	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
975	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
976	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
977	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
978	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
979	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
980	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
981	    matching is sufficient.
982	
983	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
984	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
985	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
986	
987	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
988	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
989	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
990	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
991	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
992	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
993	
994	#### Masking strategy suggestions
995	
996	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
997	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
998	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
999	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
1000	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
1001	  empty list rather than an error.
1002	
1003	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
1004	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
1005	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
1006	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
1007	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
1008	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
1009	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
1010	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
1011	
1012	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
1013	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
1014	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
1015	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
1016	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
1017	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
1018	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
1019	
1020	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
1021	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
1022	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
1023	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
1024	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
1025	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
1026	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
1027	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
1028	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
1029	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
1030	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
1031	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
1032	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
1033	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
1034	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
1035	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
1036	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
1037	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
1038	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
1039	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
1040	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
1041	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
1042	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
1043	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
1044	
1045	### Row snapshots
1046	
1047	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
1048	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
1049	
1050	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
